tags.chapter_name: General Principles and Processes of Isolation of Metals

question.text: Roasted copper pyrite on smelting with sand produces

options.text: $\mathrm{FeSiO}_{3}$ as fusible slag and $\mathrm{Cu}_{2} \mathrm{S}$ as matte
$\mathrm{CaSiO}_{3}$ as infusible slag and $\mathrm{Cu}_{2} \mathrm{O}$ as matte
$\mathrm{Ca}_{3}\left(\mathrm{PO}_{4}\right)_{2}$ as fusible slag and $\mathrm{Cu}_{2} \mathrm{S}$ as matte
$\mathrm{Fe}_{3}\left(\mathrm{PO}_{4}\right)_{2}$ as infusible slag and $\mathrm{Cu}_{2} \mathrm{S}$ as matte

solution.text:
Roasted copper pyrite on smelting with sand produces $\mathrm{FeSiO}_{3}$ as fusible slag and $\mathrm{Cu}_{2}$ S as matte
For removing the gangue, FeS, silica present in the lining of the Bessemer converter, acts as a flux and forms slag (iron silicate) on reaction with FeO.
$\mathrm{FeS}+3 \mathrm{O}_{2} \longrightarrow 2 \mathrm{FeO}+2 \mathrm{SO}_{2}$
$\mathrm{FeO}+\mathrm{SiO}_{2} \longrightarrow \mathrm{FeSiO}_{3}$
Copper matte mainly contains $\mathrm{Cu}_{2} \mathrm{S}$ and FeS.
